bibliographic.citation_apa: Bulla et al. (2025). International Journal of Retina and Vitreous, 11, 120. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40942-025-00737-7

methodology.sample_description: Twenty unedited Portuguese questions about retinal diseases from an online video channel; responses from four named chatbots and fellowship-trained retina specialists; evaluated by two independent retinal experts
methodology.technology_context: ChatGPT 4.0, ConsensusGPT, Gemini, and Claude 3 chatbots answering retinal disease patient queries compared with retina specialists

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study compares readability, accuracy, and comprehensiveness of chatbot versus specialist responses in retinal medicine and does not examine conversational governance, accountability, oversight, guardrails, audit, compliance, or related governance mechanisms.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the article involves named LLM chatbots in a regulated healthcare context, its objective and reported methods center on response-quality benchmarking against human experts rather than on governance of conversational AI systems. Governance-related content is limited to brief evaluation items on harm and ethical issues, which is insufficient for the review scope on conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Automated triage marked the record as borderline_manual because governance/accountability signals were weak while LLM and conversational terms were strong.

appraisal.notes: Methodological appraisal is based only on abstract and partial full-text excerpts provided; the article appears methodologically coherent for a comparative chatbot performance study, but this does not establish relevance to governance research questions.

cerqual.explanation: For synthesis on conversational governance, confidence is low because the available text supports claims about chatbot response quality in ophthalmology, not about governance processes, controls, or accountability structures.

coding.theme: Comparative quality of LLM chatbot responses in medical ophthalmology

synthesis.main_claim: AI chatbots can rapidly provide detailed and accurate medical information for retinal disease queries, including in non-English contexts, but some systems require higher reading levels and language simplicity should be optimized.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a blinded comparative assessment of four named chatbots against retina specialists on real unedited Portuguese patient questions using standardized expert ratings and readability metrics.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting governance evidence; at most foundational/contextual background on healthcare chatbot performance if the review separately documents non-governance clinical evaluation literature.
